items.headline: Exploited Ivanti Connect Secure chain: its root step had no fix at disclosure, and it evades the Integrity Checker

immediate_action.action: Ivanti and CISA confirm exploitation of CVE-2026-104935, and Volexity saw the chain used against a fully patched 22.8R2.4 appliance from 2026-10-03. items.summary: Ivanti disclosed CVE-2026-104935 on 2026-10-13, an authentication bypass in Connect Secure that lets a remote unauthenticated attacker run commands, and says it is aware of limited exploitation; CISA listed it in KEV the same day. Volexity found a cluster it calls UTA0576 chaining it with a root escalation that Ivanti had not fixed when Volexity reported (a separate record, CVE-2026-111357, now covers that step), patching library code in memory only so Ivanti's Integrity Checker Tool sees no file change, and going after the appliance's Active Directory service account, LAPS passwords and BitLocker recovery keys. Fixed builds are 25.1.1.2, 25.1.3.1 and 22.8R2.5 (Rapid7 also lists 25.1.3.0, which CERT-FR counts as affected); a patched appliance that was exposed still needs a compromise check, and CERT-FR says it knows of lateral movement using the LDAP and Active Directory secrets stored on the appliance and tells owners to isolate and preserve it before any reset.

items.headline: Citrix confirms in-the-wild exploitation of two default-configuration NetScaler zero-days and publishes no workaround

immediate_action.action: Citrix confirms CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88772 are being exploited against unmitigated NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway appliances right now, and Google's Mandiant reports exploitation since at least early September. CVE-2026-88771 requires no configuration at all: every default deployment is reachable by an unauthenticated attacker; CVE-2026-88772 is reachable wherever DTLS is enabled, which Citrix states is the default on any VPN virtual server. Citrix lists no workaround, and Mandiant's interim network controls (disable DTLS where it is not needed, block inbound UDP/443 upstream) cover CVE-2026-88772 only. Capture forensic evidence (logs, an instance snapshot where the appliance is virtual, a support bundle, a core dump) from each exposed appliance before patching, since the upgrade itself can destroy evidence of prior compromise, then upgrade to 14.1-73.37+ or 13.1-64.23+ (run `show ns variable` first on 13.1; if it returns any variables, install 13.1-64.24 instead to avoid a known reboot loop), going straight to 14.1-73.41+ or 13.1-64.28+ where the appliance is configured as a SAML service provider or identity provider (CVE-2026-88779), and to 14.1-73.46+ or 13.1-64.29+ where it is an identity provider (CVE-2026-107406), and run a compromise assessment on every appliance that was internet-facing.
immediate_action.title: Patch every internet-facing NetScaler ADC/Gateway now and check for pre-patch compromise

items.summary: Citrix's CTX697096 bulletin (2026-09-27) fixes eight NetScaler ADC/Gateway flaws, two of which, CVE-2026-88771 (unauthenticated command execution, every default deployment) and CVE-2026-88772 (memory overflow to RCE/DoS, reachable wherever DTLS is enabled, the VPN-vServer default), were already being exploited in the wild before any fix existed. CISA added both to KEV the same day; Citrix lists no workaround. Google's Mandiant and GTIG report a campaign running since at least early September that leaves web-server-configuration persistence on compromised appliances, so an appliance patched after the bulletin still needs a compromise check. Unit 42 telemetry adds version fingerprinting from 2026-08-21, web shells dropped as .deb packages from 2026-09-04 and a log-poisoning chain with concrete log artifacts to hunt. A separate Citrix bulletin of 2026-10-03 adds CVE-2026-88779, a SAML-triggered flaw these builds do not fix: SAML-configured appliances must move to 14.1-73.41 or 13.1-64.28, and a bulletin of 2026-10-08 adds CVE-2026-107406 for the same SAML configurations, so identity-provider appliances need 14.1-73.46 or 13.1-64.29.

items.summary: PaperCut NG and PaperCut MF (all versions) carry an unauthenticated remote-code-execution chain, CVE-2026-81578 (auth bypass, CVSS4.0 8.8) and CVE-2026-82078 (unsafe dynamic class loading, CVSS4.0 9.4), that PaperCut confirmed under active exploitation on 2026-08-27, before any CVE or patch existed. GreyNoise now documents an AI-agent-orchestrated mass-exploitation campaign against this same chain, compromising at least 440 instances across 395 identified organizations since 31 August 2026, reaching full domain admin in as little as five minutes via legacy Active Directory escalation paths. watchTowr's write-up of 2026-10-09 shows the 28 August emergency build could still be taken without authentication through the Setup Wizard forms, and names CVE-2026-82077, an administrator-only Scan-to-Fax code-execution flaw that the vendor lists as fixed in 26.0.5, 25.0.13 and 24.1.10. items.headline: Atlassian's CVE-2026-21589 record was rejected on 16 October, but the flaw, its fixes and its exploitation stand
items.summary: Atlassian's advisory of 2026-10-05 fixes CVE-2026-21589, an unauthenticated arbitrary file access flaw in every version of Bitbucket, Confluence, Jira Service Management, Jira Software, Bamboo and Crowd Data Center, plus Crucible and Fisheye (CVSS 4.0 9.3), and tells customers to patch immediately or take internet-facing instances off the internet. watchTowr Labs published the root cause, the request shape and a runnable checker on 2026-10-06, and exploitation attempts followed the same day: Previdian's honeypot sensors recorded attempts from dozens of addresses in about twenty countries, SANS ISC recorded similar attempts on its own honeypots, and a Nuclei template exists; neither honeypot operator reports a compromise. CISA added the flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-15 on evidence of active exploitation, without saying what the evidence is. Where Jira is integrated with Crowd, the file read exposes a plaintext Crowd application password that gives access to Crowd as an administrator of that application. items.headline: GTIG: AOMEI update files were altered for minutes at a time to push a backdoor; Switzerland among victim countries

actions: Audit every npm publish token your organisation and its maintainers hold and revoke any that can publish without two-factor authentication, that exact token property, not package popularity, is what decides whether the worm spreads from a compromised developer to your packages.

On any developer workstation or build agent that installed a package from the keyv family since 2026-08-04, or tensorlake@0.5.144 since 2026-10-08, treat the AI-assistant, cloud, GitHub, Vault, SSH and Kubernetes credentials present on that host as disclosed and rotate them; the collector sweeps over 300 credential patterns in one pass, so partial rotation leaves the operator a working set. Isolate the host before revoking its GitHub token, because OX Security reports a switch that wipes the machine when the token is revoked; on a host that ran tensorlake@0.5.144, Socket and OX Security also name the gh-token-monitor persistence (a systemd user unit on Linux, a LaunchAgent on macOS, a scheduled task on Windows), which has to be removed before the token is revoked.

Stop treating a valid npm provenance attestation as evidence a package is clean; where release pipelines gate on provenance, change the check to pin on the workflow identity inside the Fulcio certificate and the Rekor log index, which is what Unit 42 says still discriminates.
items.headline: A self-propagating npm worm reaches packages totalling 1.3 billion monthly downloads, and its C2 address lives on-chain
items.summary: Elastic Security Labs identified CHAINDROP on 2026-08-04, a new wave of the Shai-Hulud npm worm that began with the compromise of the keyv maintainer and has backdoored over 400 npm packages whose combined reach Elastic puts at more than 1.3 billion monthly downloads, keyv alone at over 600 million. Execution comes from a package.json preinstall hook that downloads the Bun runtime to run an obfuscated 711 KB payload, which harvests over 300 credential patterns (AI-assistant tokens, AWS/GCP/Azure/Alibaba credentials, GitHub tokens, Vault tokens, SSH keys and Kubernetes service-account tokens) and self-propagates only when it finds an npm token that both carries package-write permission and can publish without two-factor authentication. Rather than hardcoding a command-and-control domain, CHAINDROP queries an Ethereum smart contract at runtime to resolve where to send the stolen material, so the operator rotates infrastructure without shipping a new payload. On 2026-10-08 a release of the tensorlake npm SDK carried the same payload family with valid build provenance, and Socket and OX Security describe a dead-man switch that wipes the owner's home directory if the stolen GitHub token is revoked before its persistence is removed.

items.headline: FBI and Secret Service: FortiBleed is still active, locks admins out of FortiGates and feeds ransomware affiliates
items.summary: FortiBleed is an active credential-compromise campaign against internet-facing FortiGate firewalls and SSL VPN gateways, with SOCRadar counting more than 86,644 compromised devices in 194 countries; Fortinet said in June that it uses no new vulnerability, only reused credentials and brute force. A joint FBI and U.S. Secret Service advisory of 2026-10-06 says attackers keep scanning exposed devices with previously obtained credentials, create administrator accounts on compromised firewalls and in some cases delete or change the original accounts so owners are locked out, and that access brokers using the chain have supplied INC/Lynx and Payload ransomware affiliates. An organisation with an internet-exposed FortiGate should end all administrator and VPN sessions, reset every credential and look for accounts and API keys it did not create.

actions: Update Ninja Forms to 3.15.4 or later and WPC Product Bundles for WooCommerce to 8.6.7 or later on every WordPress site, then check each site for an implant the update does not remove, starting with a comparison of the database's administrator list against the Users screen and an inspection of the must-use plugins directory by content.

On any site where an administrator opened a Ninja Forms submission or a WooCommerce order since 2026-10-04 and an implant turns up, rotate all privileged credentials and the WordPress authentication salts and treat the oldest administrator account as compromised, because a login URL planted by the implant authenticates as that account.

cves.affected: Ninja Forms up to and including 3.15.3
WPC Product Bundles for WooCommerce up to and including 8.6.6

items.headline: Exploited WordPress plugin XSS ends in a hidden admin and persistence that patching does not remove
items.summary: Patchstack reports that since 2026-10-04 one campaign has been exploiting two unrelated stored cross-site scripting flaws, CVE-2026-93836 in WPC Product Bundles for WooCommerce up to 8.6.6 and CVE-2026-94504 in Ninja Forms up to 3.15.3, by planting a script in an order or a form submission that runs when a logged-in administrator opens it. The script uses the administrator's own session to install a malicious plugin and create administrators, one of them hidden from the Users screen, and leaves four independent ways back in, so updating to Ninja Forms 3.15.4 or WPC Product Bundles 8.6.7 stops new injections but does not evict an implant. Patchstack says exploitation volume is limited so far and that the second stage works with any stored XSS that reaches an administrator.

actions: Patch every PAN-OS GlobalProtect portal and gateway to the fixed release in Palo Alto's advisory for its train, or disable authentication override cookies or give them a certificate that no other service uses, then force one re-authentication so override cookies regenerate.

On every GlobalProtect gateway that was internet-reachable and unpatched at any time since 2026-05-17, treat the network behind it as a ransomware compromise-assessment target: review VPN sessions that authenticated by cookie from unexpected sources, then check Windows hosts for the artifacts Arctic Wolf describes (a ransomware payload staged under C:\\PerfLogs, a PsExec service, an LSASS dump written through comsvcs.dll to an .odt file, an ntdsutil media copy of the Active Directory database, and cleared event logs).
items.headline: CISA marks the exploited GlobalProtect VPN bypass as used in ransomware; Arctic Wolf traced Qilin intrusions to it
items.summary: CVE-2026-0257 is a pre-auth VPN authentication bypass in PAN-OS GlobalProtect (CISA KEV; Palo Alto reports limited exploit attempts, and Rapid7 and Unit 42 report successful exploitation): an attacker forges valid auth-override cookies by re-using the GlobalProtect certificate shared with the HTTPS service, with no credentials. CISA's KEV catalog (version 2026.10.04) marks it as used in known ransomware campaigns, and Arctic Wolf's report of 2026-07-20 describes June 2026 intrusions in which Qilin ransomware deployment began with this bypass. Patch or disable auth-override cookies, and treat a gateway that was exposed and unpatched as a compromise-assessment target.

actions: Upgrade every Zimbra Collaboration host to 10.1.21 (10.1.20 is the minimum for CVE-2026-73570); where the upgrade cannot happen at once, remove the zimbra-snmp package or disable SNMP notifications and restrict SNMP and SMTP to trusted hosts.

On every host that ran a build before 10.1.20 with SNMP notifications enabled at any time since 2026-07-28, upgrading is not enough: rotate all domain zimbraPreAuthKey values and run the compromise check on every mailbox node, covering the zimbra user's crontab and /opt/zimbra/.ssh/authorized_keys, JSP or stray text files under /opt/zimbra/jetty_base/webapps/zimbra/public, droppers in /tmp and /var/tmp, and outbound connections from the mail server; where web shells or an LDAP dump turn up, rotate every mailbox and administrative credential.

cves.affected: Zimbra Collaboration before 10.1.20, where the optional zimbra-snmp package is installed and SNMP notifications are enabled

items.headline: Fixed on 20 July, identified on 13 August, probed from 28 July: a CVE-keyed patch process never saw this one coming
items.summary: Zimbra shipped ZCS 10.1.20 on 2026-07-20 with a fix for a command injection in the SNMP monitoring component, and the identifier CVE-2026-73570 followed on 2026-08-13. Microsoft Threat Intelligence now reports confirmed intrusions in more than one region and industry, with probing of the injection point from 2026-07-28, before disclosure, and CISA lists the flaw in KEV (added 2026-08-21). The flaw needs no authentication and applies only where the optional zimbra-snmp package is installed and SNMP notifications are enabled; Microsoft's cases combined web shells, root escalation, theft of Zimbra's authentication keys and cluster-wide movement, so an upgrade does not evict an attacker already inside. CSIRT Italia reports that exploitation of this flaw has also led to ELock-family ransomware, cryptomining and theft of the LDAP database and credential hashes on exposed servers, and found no intrusion on regularly updated instances.

actions: Install the October 2026 Exchange security update on every Exchange server and on every machine that has the Exchange Management Tools; on Exchange 2016 and 2019 servers that are not covered by the Period 2 ESU, decide now between enrolling (it only gets an organisation current through this release) and moving to Exchange Subscription Edition, because after October Microsoft ships updates for Subscription Edition only.

On every Exchange server that has the October 2026 Windows Server update installed, do not uninstall it; where OWA fails with MapiExceptionMdbOffline, mail queues grow or a DAG member cannot reach quorum, set the registry value EpmapSavedContextCap (REG_DWORD) under HKLM\\SOFTWARE\\Microsoft\\Rpc to 65536, reboot, and raise the limit if the failure recurs.

Exchange Server Subscription Edition, 2019 CU14 and CU15, 2016 CU23 (builds before the October 2026 updates)

items.headline: Exchange October updates fix an unauthenticated email-borne RCE; 2016 and 2019 get their last update, and only with ESU
items.summary: Microsoft's 2026-10-13 Exchange security updates fix CVE-2026-70571, a stack-based buffer overflow that an unauthenticated attacker can trigger with a crafted email (Critical, CVSS 8.1 with high attack complexity, Exploitation More Likely, not exploited), and CVE-2026-70279, a 9.3 cross-site scripting flaw that lets an attacker act as an administrator who clicks a crafted link. October is the last month Exchange 2016 and 2019 customers enrolled in the Period 2 ESU receive newly released updates, and organisations without ESU have no 2016 or 2019 update at all. Microsoft's Exchange Team says the October Windows Server updates (KB5126646, KB5126655, KB5126651, KB5126868) can make Exchange servers unstable, with OWA failures, growing mail queues and lost DAG quorum, whether or not the Exchange update is installed; it advises against uninstalling them and on 2026-10-17 gave a registry workaround.

actions: Tell the helpdesk, HR and payroll teams of every body whose staff are insured with Publica (including the federal administration and the ETH domain) or with the Pensionskasse Stadt Zürich, which says data of its insured persons and pensioners was stolen, that AHV number, date of birth, address, salary and IBAN may now be known to criminals and must not count as proof of identity, and route requests that quote them, a request to change a payout account included, to a call-back on a known number; for staff insured with Pensionskasse Post, the Bernische Pensionskasse or the Bernische Lehrerversicherungskasse apply the same rule until those funds report the scope; also tell insured staff that cantonal police warn of investment-fraud calls from people who know their salary and pension details, which prove nothing about the caller.

If your organisation's pension administration, HR or payroll runs on PK Softech software, is being migrated to it or tested on it, or your staff are insured with Pensionskasse Post, ask the supplier or the fund in writing whether your data, test data included, was in the affected environment and what it holds.
items.headline: PK Softech: the City of Zurich pension fund confirms its test data was stolen; Pensionskasse Post says data left
items.summary: The Confederation, in a release headlined "data outflow confirmed", said on 2026-10-08 that a software supplier of Publica detected a cyberattack at the end of September, and the supplier PK Softech AG (Reinach BL) says unknown attackers used malware to reach part of its IT infrastructure and that it must be assumed data left its systems; the Federal Prosecutor's Office is investigating. Publica insures, among others, staff of the federal administration and the ETH domain, about 70,000 active members and 41,600 pensioners at the end of 2025, and says personal data of insured persons has presumably left, while the AWP agency relays the supplier's position that the volume is rather small and the data may be business data. The Pensionskasse Stadt Zürich now says personal data of its insured persons and pensioners, handed to PK Softech as test data for a planned 2027 switch to its system, was stolen, and Pensionskasse Post says personal data did leave but not yet whether its insured persons' data is among it; the Bernische Pensionskasse has no indication of theft but cannot exclude it and the Bernische Lehrerversicherungskasse is still checking. Which fields were taken is still being clarified by each fund, and the access vector and the actor are not public. Cantonal police warn that criminals could use leaked salary and pension data for investment-fraud calls, and the Zurich cantonal fund BVK, a customer since 2011, says it runs the software in its own data centre and is not directly affected.

items.headline: Adobe fixes unauthenticated CVSS 10.0 flaws in ColdFusion, Experience Manager and Commerce; no exploitation known
items.summary: Adobe's 2026-10-13 bulletins fix five unauthenticated network flaws at CVSS 9.0 to 10.0 in ColdFusion 2025 and 2023 (fixed in 2025.0.14 and 2023.0.26), three unauthenticated CVSS 10.0 code-execution flaws in Experience Manager (Cloud Service 2026.9.28386 or per-issue hotfixes) and two code-execution flaws (CVSS 10.0 and 9.8) in Adobe Commerce and Magento Open Source (2026-oct builds). Adobe says it knows of no exploitation of any of them; each needs no account, so exposure rather than exploitation status decides the order. Sansec reproduced four code-execution routes for the Commerce flaw CVE-2026-103849 within 24 hours of the fix, sees no exploitation yet, and warns that a Composer install keeps the vulnerable base version until the 2026-oct release or Adobe's isolated patch is applied.

actions: Find every WordPress site that your organisation, its web agencies or its hosting suppliers run with Bricksforge and update it to version 4.0.1 (3.1.8.10 on the 3.x line) now, treating any site that was reachable and unpatched since 2026-10-07 as one to search for dropped PHP files.

items.headline: Bricksforge's Pro Forms upload flaw is exploited without login since 7 October; fixed in 4.0.1 and 3.1.8.10
items.summary: Patchstack reports that CVE-2026-85097, an unauthenticated arbitrary file upload in the Pro Forms module of Bricksforge, a paid WordPress add-on for the Bricks page builder, has been targeted in the wild since 2026-10-07: it lets an attacker with no account get a PHP file written to the uploads directory and executed, on versions up to and including 3.1.8.9 with Pro Forms active (about 6,000 active installations). Bricksforge's changelog of 2026-10-08 lists the fix in 4.0.1 and Patchstack names 3.1.8.10 for the 3.x line; the exploitation report rests on Patchstack's telemetry.

actions: Run an organisation-scoped GitHub code search in every organisation your teams and suppliers administer for workflow files under .github/workflows that present themselves as a security audit, a security check or an Actions security workflow and were added since 2026-08-31; any hit means assume breach: revoke the credential that committed it and rotate every secret found anywhere in the repository's git history, not only the configured Actions secrets.
items.headline: GhostAction: fake security workflows now harvest whole git histories; rotating Actions secrets is not enough
items.summary: StepSecurity and Socket report that on 2026-10-08 the GhostAction campaign used the GitHub credentials of two open-source maintainers to commit a workflow disguised as a security audit straight to the default branch of 345 to 346 repositories, including one of an Uber-owned organisation, and that the workflow now sends the credentials found in the working tree and in the entire git history, besides the named Actions secrets, to a hardcoded address over plain HTTP. StepSecurity read a run log showing the exfiltration was acknowledged four seconds after the run started; no malicious package release from the stolen credentials has been seen yet.

items.headline: Citrix: a new NetScaler SAML overflow, rated Critical, reaches the builds that fixed the previous one
items.summary: Citrix's bulletin CTX697191 (2026-10-08, severity Critical) fixes CVE-2026-107406, a memory overflow in customer-managed NetScaler ADC and Gateway that leads to remote code execution or denial of service (CVSS 4.0 9.5) when the appliance is configured as a SAML service provider or identity provider. An identity-provider appliance is affected through the 14.1-73.41 and 13.1-64.28 builds that Citrix named for CVE-2026-88779 and must move to 14.1-73.46, 13.1-64.29 or the FIPS builds; Citrix says it is not aware of any unmitigated exploits.

actions: If your organisation bought video-surveillance, alarm or access-control installation or maintenance from Ixa Systems, ask the firm in writing which of your sites and credentials are in the stolen data and rotate every camera, alarm, intercom and remote-maintenance credential it held.
items.headline: Site plans, camera locations and some credentials of Vaud prisons and banks, and of police premises, reported for sale
items.summary: Le Temps reports, and the AWP news agency names the firm as Ixa Systems of Crissier (Vaud), that data stolen from a video-surveillance, alarm and access-control integrator is on sale on the darknet; the group TheGentlemen claimed the theft at the end of August. The loot reportedly includes camera locations, security-installation plans and, in some cases, usernames or passwords, for clients including police authorities, gendarmerie premises, prisons, hospitals, schools and banks; the reports do not state the access vector or list every affected site.

actions: Find every RouterOS device whose www or www-ssl service answers from a network you do not trust and upgrade it to the fixed build for its channel: 7.24 or later on v7 stable, 7.23.8 on v7 long-term, 6.49.23 on v6 long-term; where an upgrade has to wait, restrict www and www-ssl under IP > Services to trusted addresses or disable them and manage the router over WinBox, SSH or a VPN.

items.headline: MikroTik's long-term changelogs already carry the fix for a pre-auth RouterOS RCE; its notice still says pending
items.summary: MikroTik's notice of 2026-10-06 describes CVE-2026-84411, an integer underflow in HTTP request body handling of the RouterOS web management service (WebFig, on the www and www-ssl ports) that one crafted request sent without logging in can use to crash the service or run code on the router with full privileges; CISA scores it CVSS 3.1 9.8. RouterOS before 7.24, v6 included, is affected where an attacker can reach the web interface; 7.24 fixes the v7 stable channel and MikroTik's changelogs list the fix in 7.23.8 (v7 long-term, 2026-10-08) and 6.49.23 (v6 long-term, 2026-10-07), although its notice still shows both long-term releases as pending; MikroTik says the default firewall already blocks the web interface from the internet, and CISA records no known public exploitation.
